text:
gabe_support: Customer reported brief 429s during an hourly backfill despite their burst credits showing ~80% available in the console. They saw ~90s of errors, started at ~2026-03-16T08:12:05Z. stack: Dedicated (reserved), model redwood/gpt-small-8q, client concurrency ~40. Can we triage?

maria_eng: Can you paste account id + a sample request id and exact UTC range? Was this single route or many? Any trace ids?

gabe_support: Account 98765, sample req_id req_0a1b2c. Fail window 2026-03-16T08:12:05Z -> 2026-03-16T08:13:38Z. They were doing a parallel job: 200 small prompts, max_tokens=64, client parallelism 40. Error payload looked like `{"error":"429","code":"quota_exceeded","detail":"burst cushion exhausted"}`. Attached their condensed logs.

rate-limiter-bot: Observability note: burst_credits for acct 98765 dropped to ~0 at 08:12:04Z, fractional refill shows 0.6 -> 1.2 credits over next 60s (lag observed). Peak concurrent inflight requests ~38. Token drain spike at 08:12:03Z.

jon_ops: Quick explainer (tl;dr): burst credits are a short-term cushion but smoothing and concurrency limits interact. Two likely causes: 1) simultaneous parallel requests created per-request token bursts that exhausted the cushion faster than console's coarse metric — console can lag by a few seconds. 2) fractional refill (we top-up credits on a rolling window) plus our smoothing window means a very short, high-concurrency burst can hit zero and produce transient 429s even if the hourly/console view shows available credit.

maria_eng: Also note route-level concurrency and per-account inflight thresholds still apply. If many requests start at same millisecond you'll hit a concurrency check before refill can help.

sara_support: For immediate customer guidance: 1) Reduce client concurrency to ~15-20 for this backfill pattern. 2) Add small random jitter and exponential backoff on 429s (retry after 100-300ms jitter). 3) If they need a short-term lift, we can provision a 1-hour reserved capacity bump while they re-run the backfill. Do we want to propose that?

gabe_support: I'll offer the 1-hour bump + recommend concurrency throttling and jitter. Also sending a sample repro script to help them test locally.

maria_eng: Repro snippet to emulate their pattern (share this with the customer):

```
# simulate parallel backfill
python3 - <<'PY'
import requests, time, threading
url = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate'
headers = {'Authorization':'Bearer REDACTED'}
concurrency = 40
requests_per_worker = 5
payload = {'model':'redwood/gpt-small-8q','input':'short prompt','max_tokens':64}

def worker():
    for _ in range(requests_per_worker):
        r = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
        print(r.status_code, r.text[:80])

threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker) for _ in range(concurrency)]
start=time.time()
for t in threads: t.start()
for t in threads: t.join()
print('elapsed', time.time()-start)
PY
```

jon_ops: Ops note: we should add a dashboard tile exposing "fractional refill rate" and a per-route short-window credit metric (1s/5s) so support can correlate faster. Filing a follow-up ticket.

maria_eng: Filing ticket: ENG-xxxxx to consider smoothing-window tuning and dashboard visibility. Also flag for possible optimization where console shows near-real-time credits (currently ~3-5s lag).

gabe_support: Oncall notified and customer update queued. I'll offer the temporary bump and the concurrency/jitter guidance. Thanks everyone.

jon_ops: +1 on the bump. Keep thread updated with customer outcome. :thumbsup:
